content.user_title: Choose Apple Selection and Input Controls
content.value_statement: Choosing the wrong Apple control creates confusing state, input, and accessibility behavior. This skill recommends suitable controls and explains state management, validation, platform fit, and VoiceOver considerations.
actual_capabilities: Recommends controls based on data type, option count, platform, and interface context.
Compares toggles, segmented controls, sliders, pickers, steppers, text fields, combo boxes, token fields, gauges, and rating indicators.
Explains how selection state appears and when changes apply.
Suggests validation timing and communication for selection and text input.
Provides accessibility guidance for labels, traits, hints, focus, and VoiceOver.
limitations: Provides design guidance but does not implement or test interface code.
Focuses on Apple platforms and does not cover other design systems.
Needs product context to choose among controls with similar behavior.
Does not replace current Apple documentation, platform testing, or accessibility review.

use_cases.title: Plan a settings screen
use_cases.description: Select clear controls for binary settings, fixed choices, ranges, and text input.

use_cases.title: Review an Apple form
use_cases.description: Check control selection, state commitment, validation timing, and platform conventions before implementation.

use_cases.title: Audit control accessibility
use_cases.description: Identify missing labels, unclear states, focus conflicts, and VoiceOver considerations across input workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Select a control
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend an Apple control for [data type] with [option count] options on [platform]. Explain the choice and one unsuitable alternative.

prompt_templates.title: Review an existing form
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Apple form: [description]. Identify control mismatches, state issues, validation timing, and accessibility gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Design a cross-platform flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design selection and input controls for [workflow] across [platforms]. Address control variants, state commitment, keyboard behavior, validation, and VoiceOver.

prompt_templates.title: Compare complex control strategies
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare at least three control strategies for [complex requirement]. Recommend one using option scale, precision, platform conventions, accessibility, and error recovery.

output_examples.input: Users need to enable automatic downloads in an iOS settings screen.
output: Recommendation: Use a switch because the setting is binary and takes effect immediately.
State: Show a clear on or off state and keep the label focused on the setting.
Accessibility: Provide a descriptive label and expose the current state to VoiceOver.

output_examples.input: Users adjust text size within a broad range, and exact values are not important.
output: Recommendation: Use a slider because the value is continuous and precision is not critical.
Range: Add meaningful endpoint labels or icons and present the selected value when useful.
Alternative: Use a stepper only when users need small, precise increments.

output_examples.input: A macOS compose window accepts several email recipients and supports address suggestions.
output: Recommendation: Use a token field to represent each recipient as a discrete value.
Interaction: Support suggestions, clear selection, editing, and removal of individual recipients.
Accessibility: Give each token a meaningful label and predictable keyboard focus.

best_practices: Describe the data type, option count, platform, and where the control appears.
State whether changes apply immediately or after confirmation.
Validate recommendations against current Apple guidance and test with assistive technologies.
anti_patterns: Do not use segmented controls for long or unequal option lists.
Do not rely on color alone to communicate state.
Do not request a custom control when a standard control meets the requirement.

faq.question: Which platforms does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It focuses on Apple platform controls and notes platform-specific differences when the references provide them.

faq.question: Does this skill generate interface code?
faq.answer: No. It provides control recommendations and design guidance that developers can apply in their chosen framework.

faq.question: Which controls can it compare?
faq.answer: It covers toggles, segmented controls, sliders, steppers, pickers, text inputs, combo boxes, token fields, gauges, and rating indicators.

faq.question: What context improves a recommendation?
faq.answer: Provide the data type, option count, Apple platform, interface location, and whether changes apply immediately.

faq.question: Does it address accessibility?
faq.answer: Yes. Recommendations can cover labels, visible state, focus placement, traits, hints, keyboard behavior, and VoiceOver.

faq.question: Does it replace official Apple guidance?
faq.answer: No. Verify current requirements in Apple documentation and test the final interface on supported platforms.
